items.stem: In standard synchronous data-parallel training, what does the all-reduce step accomplish each iteration?

options.text: It averages the gradients computed on every worker so all replicas apply the same update
options.rationale: Correct: all-reduce sums/averages per-worker gradients so model replicas stay identical.

options.text: It copies the full dataset to every worker before the forward pass
options.rationale: Data sharding, not all-reduce, distributes data; all-reduce exchanges gradients.

options.text: It splits the model layers across workers
options.rationale: That is model/pipeline parallelism, not the all-reduce of data parallelism.

options.text: It compresses the model weights for storage
options.rationale: All-reduce synchronises gradients; it is not a storage-compression step.

items.explanation: Correct: all-reduce sums/averages per-worker gradients so model replicas stay identical.

items.stem: Which TWO conditions most strongly favour tensor/sharded parallelism (e.g. FSDP/ZeRO) over plain data parallelism? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The model's parameters and optimiser state exceed a single device's memory
options.rationale: Correct: sharding the state across devices is the main reason to use FSDP/ZeRO.

options.text: A high-bandwidth interconnect is available between devices
options.rationale: Correct: sharded parallelism exchanges more data, so it relies on fast interconnect.

options.text: The model is tiny and fits easily on one GPU
options.rationale: A small model needs no sharding; data parallelism suffices.

options.text: There is no network between the workers
options.rationale: Sharded parallelism requires frequent communication; no network makes it unworkable.

items.explanation: Correct: sharding the state across devices is the main reason to use FSDP/ZeRO.

items.stem: A multi-day run uses preemptible nodes that can disappear at any time. What is the most important mitigation?

options.text: Checkpoint model and optimiser state frequently so training can resume
options.rationale: Correct: frequent checkpointing bounds the work lost when a node is preempted.

options.text: Disable logging to save disk space
options.rationale: Logging is unrelated to surviving preemption and aids diagnosis.
Learning rate does not address node loss.

options.text: Train on a single node only
options.rationale: That may avoid preemption but defeats the need to train at scale.

items.explanation: Correct: frequent checkpointing bounds the work lost when a node is preempted.
